name: pdc-cptac-stad-study
description:
The CPTAC gastric cancer study is the most extensively measured cohort indexed here. Four of its seven layers - acetylome, glycoproteome, ubiquitylome and metabolome - exist in fewer than twenty NCI cohorts each, and the combination on a single set of 193 tumors exists nowhere else. Ubiquitylation data on 184 cases is particularly scarce: only five studies in the entire Proteomic Data Commons carry it.
It is also a clear illustration of why reuse measurement is hard. All of it is openly downloadable with no account, and yet a literature search for its accession finds almost nothing - because authors cite the marker paper, not the PDC study identifier. The absence of citation evidence here says more about how proteomics data are referenced than about whether anyone has used them.
citeAs: A 15-layer multi-omics analysis of gastric cancer ecotypes provides therapeutic insights.

recordSet.name: Clinical variables with measured completeness
recordSet.description: Completeness is measured from the source repository's own records. A field populated entirely with non-answers is reported as populated but not informative, because it blocks an analysis just as surely as an absent field.

supportedQuestions: How do distinct post-translational modification layers diverge from each other and from transcript abundance on the same tumors?
Does protein degradation signaling, read from the ubiquitylome, identify tumor subgroups invisible to transcriptomics?
How does tumor metabolism, measured directly rather than inferred, relate to signaling state?
Can measured protein-protein interaction data improve network inference over correlation-based approaches?

blockingLimitations.statement: The PDC record carries no clinical annotation: no survival, no treatment, no stage and no demographics are exposed through the study metadata.

inappropriateUses: Survival or prognostic analysis using PDC data alone.
Treating the seven layers as a complete-case multi-omic matrix without checking overlap.
